tasks.short: Hand out product samples or literature on the round

steps.what: Take the day's product samples and literature
Choose a sample or literature for this person
Hand that sample or literature to the person

tasks.design: She still collects the samples and literature, chooses who receives one, and hands it over in person. That visit is the task. Nothing in it moves to a machine.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is the handout on the street, and the person in front of her decides whether to take it.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes that visit. A stack of literature was already printed before she left.
tasks.still_hard: Who is willing to take a sample, and saying what it is without a script doing the talking.
tasks.human_edge: She sees who is in a hurry, who already has the leaflet, and who might want the sample.
tasks.altitude: Her week on this task does not change. She still carries the stock and hands it out.

reach.task: Hand the goods across once they are paid for
reach.learn: Which sample may leave her hands before any payment

evidence.claim: Handing out samples or literature is the visit itself. Model knowledge, grade E1. No system in the digest performs that handout.

assumptions: The literature and samples already exist when she starts. Packing them is part of taking the stock, and it stays physical.
No extra upkeep is counted. There is no machine to keep, and the handout is not a message that is sent later.
unknowns: Whether a colleague pre-packs her bag before the round, or she takes the stock herself.
research_questions: What share of this task is carrying and handing, against choosing which piece to offer?

already_counted.description: Collecting, choosing and handing all stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: No extra upkeep. The handout stays a visit.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The visit is unchanged, so the saved share of this task is zero on a short round and on a long one.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Travel the round to deliver or sell merchandise

steps.what: List customers and streets for today's travel
Order those streets into a shorter travel route
Change a travel order that cannot deliver on time
Travel the round and deliver the merchandise

tasks.design: She lists each stop as a street and any time she must arrive. A distance order in {OTHER} drafts a shorter travel sequence from that list. She moves any stop that would miss a time she promised, then walks, cycles or drives the round herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The order of stops lived in her head, and a promised arrival is not the same as a shorter distance.
tasks.enabler_now: A street and a time are enough for a distance order she can still reject.
tasks.still_hard: A person who is out, a street she will not use, and selling or delivering once she is there.
tasks.human_edge: She decides who is on the round, and whether a promised time beats the shorter travel.
tasks.altitude: She still travels and delivers. She no longer redraws the street order by hand. She does not gain the right to skip a stop she promised.

reach.task: Visit a site to drop off a part
reach.learn: How a street and a must-arrive time are written so a later order can use them

evidence.claim: Ordering known streets by distance is arithmetic once each stop has a street. Model knowledge, grade E1. The digest names no route product for this work.
A round list that stores a customer's name needs a lawful basis the company already has for that person. Model knowledge, grade E1.

assumptions: Each stop she wants ordered has a street and either a must-arrive time or an empty time. She writes both in the list step. A stop with no street stays off the order and she places it while she checks.
No route tool is in use today, so the order is new code over her list, not a setting in a system she already runs.
No extra upkeep is counted. Fixing a bad order is the check step, which keeps its full time. A customer name, when she stores one, uses a lawful basis the company already holds.
unknowns: Whether today's list is streets only, or also customer names.
How often a promised time forces her to ignore the shorter order.
research_questions: What share of the round is spent deciding the street order, against travelling and delivering?

already_counted.description: Listing stops, fixing a bad order, and travelling stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: No extra upkeep beyond the check she already does.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a short street the order is obvious, so little of the sorting time was real. Stops with no street stay unsorted. A day of timed deliveries keeps most of the check.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Persuade customers to purchase merchandise or services

steps.what: Hear what customers want before any purchase
Choose merchandise that matches what customers said
Persuade customers to purchase that merchandise

tasks.design: She listens, chooses the merchandise, and asks the person to buy. That conversation stays hers. No draft pitch is prepared for her to read out.
tasks.previous_blocker: The sale depends on the person in front of her, and the reason to buy changes with each conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new carries that conversation. A fixed set of prices was already known before she spoke.
tasks.still_hard: Reading whether the person will buy, and stopping when they will not.
tasks.human_edge: She hears the objection, changes the offer, and decides when to stop asking.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes on this task. She still makes the sale herself.

reach.task: Take payment after the person agrees to buy
reach.learn: Where her ask ends and the cashier's payment begins

evidence.claim: Persuading a person at the door or on the street stays a conversation. Model knowledge, grade E1. The digest keeps selling with a person and cites no street-selling case.

assumptions: The ask is the live conversation, not a message sent afterwards, so there is no separate release to gate.
No extra upkeep is counted. There is no tool to maintain, and she does not store a script.
unknowns: Whether she may offer a discount on the spot, or the price is fixed before she leaves.
research_questions: How often the person buys at the first ask, against a second visit?

already_counted.description: Listening, choosing and persuading stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: No extra upkeep. The conversation stays hers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conversation is unchanged, on a willing customer and on one who refuses.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order or purchase the supplies for the round

steps.what: Count the supplies still on hand
Decide which supplies to purchase and how many
Draft the supply order from those lines
Check the draft against the supplies counted
Approve that supply order before it goes out
Send the approved supply order to the supplier

tasks.design: She counts what is left and names the item and the quantity. {PROCUREMENT} drafts the supply order from those lines. She corrects it, the sales supervisor releases that version, and only then {PROCUREMENT} sends it. A line she did not count is not sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: The order was a note or a phone call, so the item and the quantity were not fields a purchasing record could fill.
tasks.enabler_now: Item and quantity are enough for a draft. The release to the supplier stays a person's decision on that version.
tasks.still_hard: Goods that are not in the catalogue, a supplier who only takes a phone call, and judging how much the next round will use.
tasks.human_edge: She sets the quantity from how the round is going. The sales supervisor decides whether the company should buy it.

ambition.what: Place a supply order the day a line runs short

tasks.altitude: She stops retyping the order. She still chooses quantities. She does not release an outside order on her own.

reach.task: Reorder a part the counter is short of
reach.learn: The item and quantity fields, and that the send waits for a released version

evidence.claim: A purchasing record can be filled from an item and a quantity, and can send only a version a person has released. Model knowledge, grade E1. No digest case is about street-seller supplies.

assumptions: A line she wants drafted has an item already in the purchasing catalogue and a quantity. She writes both while she counts and decides. A missing item is not drafted.
Phoning a supplier for an off-catalogue item is the incremental allowance. It is not a second pass through the send, and it is not already inside the check.

Outside supply orders wait for the sales supervisor. That reading is other-role time in the approval step. The street seller places the order today, so the send remains her step. A later change to the lines voids the release.
unknowns: Whether the company already records supply orders in a purchasing system, or only by phone.
Whether the sales supervisor or the street seller is the person who may release an outside order.
research_questions: What share of supply orders are catalogue lines, against a phone call to a wholesaler?

already_counted.description: Counting, choosing quantities and correcting the draft stay in her remaining time.
The sales supervisor reads the corrected order before it can be sent.

incremental.description: Phone the supplier when a line is not in the catalogue or the order is rejected.

approvals.approved_version: corrected supply order the sales supervisor released

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A month of phone-only wholesaler orders keeps the typing and the call. A month of catalogue lines removes both, and the supervisor still releases each order. Off-catalogue rework is already taken off.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Samples, the round and the sale stay with the street seller. She gets a shorter walking order and a supply draft she does not retype. She still chooses who she visits and what she says. An outside supply order still waits for the sales supervisor.
skills_to_grow: Write each stop as a street plus any time she must arrive
Reject a walking order that misses a time she promised
Count supplies before a draft, and do not confirm a line she did not count
role.ambitious_version: A later version could refill a regular supply line once the sales supervisor has released that item and quantity. It would still not walk the round, hand out samples, persuade a customer, or send an order that has not been released.

job.title: Door-to-Door Sales Workers, News and Street Vendors, and Related Workers
